template.name: Single-bridge Galerkin operator and schedule timing
template.eligibility: Before freeze, require independently verified 18/18 switch qualification at 21 snapshots, all fixed-rate Galerkin controls, and the preregistered FD176 CPU/GPU qualification at all 19 physical times. Both physical references and their budget remain fixed. Every timed row must meet the two physical references, the same-schedule implementation field and probe gates, and sustained alternate wake shedding. Retain the switch triangle guard at the 19 common physical times. A failed arm stays in the journal and prevents an isolated matched-accuracy claim for the cohort.
template.time_scope: One fresh Python child per registered job. Record solver seconds including model, basis and factors, CUDA context, upload, FFT plans and priming, graph capture, full march and observations, synchronization, download and solver resource cleanup. Measure final release of the solver model separately and include it in solver seconds. Also record parent Popen-to-flushed completion marker time, including Python startup/imports and brief result bookkeeping, before the child serializes its trajectory. The parent waits for complete child exit, scoring and artifact writes before starting the next job. Keep the operating-system and driver caches in their current state.
template.isolation_scope: One complete randomized 60-row attempt. Two consecutive quiet 10-second preflight windows, then the full fixed 900-second monitored window, including imports, reference preparation, all scoring and serialization. Preserve external-load or incomplete attempts as diagnostic evidence. No retries, replacement arms or combination with the previous 50-row cohorts. The monitor recognizes the coordinator and its registered serial children and samples external Python activity and endpoint GPU utilization. Its observations cover sampled Python processes and aggregate GPU utilization at the endpoints.
template.planned_window_basis: Existing diagnostic solver samples project 389 seconds by arm medians and 402 seconds by summed per-arm maxima. Earlier 50-row execution spent 50-53 additional seconds on setup outside the solver, scoring and storage. Conservatively scaling that overhead by (60/50)*(19/7) projects about 554-575 seconds before new process startup. The one independent T9 transport exercise added about 1.99 seconds before the completion marker. A planning allowance of 1.5-2.5 seconds for each of sixty starts projects about 644-725 seconds for the complete worker. These numbers plan the window only.

template.name: Independent three-scale FD4 qualification at all common physical checkpoints
template.scope: Accuracy qualification only. All original physical times are shared by CPU, CUDA and both references. No phase alignment or time interpolation. Each FD radial resolution is independent and failures are retained. Concurrent solver durations are diagnostic and not an isolated timing comparison.

early_reference_protocol.name: T16 independent startup reference continuation
early_reference_protocol.scope: Continue the four frozen T8 arms from their complete T6 SBDF2 histories. Preserve the archived original checkpoints. Only the continuation identity step total, snapshot schedule and probe capacity change. Require exact original states and probes through T8 before auditing any continuation. Use the same empirical independent-axis budget at all twelve common times. Accuracy only.
